scope: Numerical validity contract only; prior failed result stays failed. Scientific sampling, .2 near coefficient, loss reductions, model mode and descriptive decision rules are byte-identical in copied PLAN/sampling.
diagnosis: Same-graph repeat is bitwise identical; output loss derivatives differ at FP32 rounding scale; full-network reconstruction differences are deterministic finite-precision backward non-distributivity. Full genuinely double forward/loss/backward reconstructs at about 1e-15 relative L2. FP64 aggregation of already computed FP32 component gradients does not fix it. No objective/ordering/accumulation/mutation defect found.

old_elementwise_rule.treatment: Record every failure and maximum allowance ratio; never relabel original attempt as passing. Unsuitable as sole high-dimensional directional validity criterion near cancellation; failure not solely at exact zeros.

new_joint_checks.relative_L2_definition: norm64(actual-reconstructed)/norm64(actual) for encoder, decoder (includes head), head; exact-zero actual requires exact-zero reconstruction
new_joint_checks.cosine_reference: Compare cos(actual,near_MAE) and cos(reconstructed,near_MAE); both undefined only when norms <=1e-12
new_joint_checks.classification_stability: Direct and reconstructed current/candidate gradients must agree on original conflict<-0.05, candidate improvement>=0.05, near-partition/current<=0.10 and weighted-near/current>=0.10 classifications. Scientific cutoffs/counts/breadth remain unchanged.
new_joint_checks.on_failure: Stop this sole rerun. No new amendment, resampling, precision change, threshold relaxation, or further probe.

justification: 1e-5 relative L2 is a declared 0.001% vector error ceiling, tighter than original 1e-4 relative coefficient, paired with a maximum-element outlier safeguard and independently checked directional/classification effects. It is a change of error metric, not a larger pointwise tolerance. For nonzero vectors relative perturbation delta gives directional cosine error bounded by about 2*delta/(1-delta), far smaller than the 0.05 scientific effect. Observed FP32 reconstruction errors were <=1.45e-6, cosine changes <=1.1e-7; genuine FP64 reconstruction <=1.8e-15. This is empirically reference-supported, not a formal bound for every network/batch. Full-forward FP32 vs FP64 cosine shift reached 2.30e-4, showing piecewise-network precision sensitivity beyond reconstruction; no sampled first-two scientific classifications changed. This limitation remains explicit.
authorization: Current user permits a reference-supported revised numerical check, frozen before remaining batches. At most one original 64-frame rerun, within combined 1800-second numerical budget.
